basis: Psychiatric eating-disorder umbrella; physiological complications do not establish common direct organ damage across the group.
Autoimmune inflammation directly damages the liver; concurrent autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Malignant neoplasm involving the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
GATA4-related atrial septal defect; reported associated malformations also affect the cardiovascular axis.
Endocrine delta-cell tumor arising in pancreas (~60%) or intestine (~40%); direct gallbladder dysfunction occurs in 30-79%; anemia lacks evidence of direct blood-cell damage.
Preeclampsia is defined by hypertension with renal endothelial injury/proteinuria or other organ dysfunction; eclamptic neurologic injury affects a minority.
Arthrogryposis with lissencephaly defines congenital joint contractures and abnormal brain development.
Progressive upper motor neuron degeneration; weakness, spasticity and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than separate muscle or gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital malformation with an abnormal communication between bronchopulmonary tissue and the esophagus or stomach.
Adenoma arising in the vagina; reproductive tissue has no applicable axis.
Immunodeficiency with encephalopathy/seizures in 4/4, liver dysfunction in 100% with frequent fibrosis, and functional hyposplenia supported by Howell-Jolly bodies in 2/2.
Malignant renal tubular epithelial tumor presenting as a cystic renal mass.
Mixed inhaled dust causes pneumoconiosis with direct interstitial lung injury.
Inherited surfactant metabolism dysfunction causes alveolar surfactant accumulation and chronic respiratory impairment.
Intellectual disability, gingival overgrowth and absent nails define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss in 1/2; kyphosis in 1/2 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Primary CNS astrocytic tumor arising near the lateral ventricles; associated tuberous sclerosis is a separate disease.
Limb anomalies, deafness and pigmentary defects define WS3; structural blepharophimosis occurs in 80-99%; atelectasis reported in 30-79% omitted at cap.
Paralysis of laryngeal abductors directly impairs the upper airway; additional neurologic disease is not established as common.
Syndrome defined by intellectual disability and growth hormone deficiency; both occur in 80-99%. Other structural findings are occasional.
Focal or multifocal neuronal migration defects are developmental malformations of the brain.
Ovarian epithelial tumor of reproductive tissue; endocrine origin or hormone dysfunction is not established.
Core intellectual disability; ptosis in 18/20, AV canal defects and hearing loss each 30-79%; limb and palatal malformations omitted at the four-axis cap.
Inflammation directly affects the vestibular cranial nerve and vestibular function; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not established.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia; joint contracture, sensorineural hearing loss and myopia each reported in 1/1; frequency estimates are limited by the single case.
Marrow failure, nail/skin changes and oral leukoplakia define dyskeratosis congenita; cirrhosis in 1/2; neurologic and immune findings omitted at the four-axis cap.
